newsitem.title: UK: Bass very disappointed by block of merger.
newsitem.headline: Bass very disappointed by block of merger.

text.p: UK brewing giant Bass Plc said on Friday it was "extremely disappointed" with the government's decision to block its proposed merger with Carlsberg-Tetley.
It pledged to continue to build on its brewing business success at home and abroad.

The group made the statement after Margaret Beckett, Trade and Industry Secretary, ruled out the merger on the grounds that even divestment of 1,900 Bass pubs would not be enough to allay her competition concerns.
A Bass spokesman told Reuters: "It was a resounding 'no' and there's not a lot we can do about it."

The Bass spokesman said the group would be in talks with UK competition watchdog the Office of Fair Trading (OFT) over coming weeks on the government requirement to dispose of its 50-percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley.

"We are now discussing with the OFT how to dispose of the shares," he said. Commenting on the net cost of the failed merger, Bass said it should be in the region of 60 million stg before accounting for Bass' share of Carlsberg-Tetley profits, dividends and royalties.
Asked about the way forward now, he added: "We will continue to develop market share organically. We have strong brands and are one of the most cost-effective producers in the UK drinks sector."
Bass said it did not anticipate a jobs fallout now that the merger had failed. "From our point of view that is unlikely. But it could be a question for Carlsberg-Tetley," said the Bass spokesman.

Bass admitted it was confused about why Beckett had ruled out the deal which would have made it Britain's biggest brewer, despite suggestions by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission that a divestment of 1,900 Bass pubs could be a way forward.

"We don't know what caused Margaret Beckett to take that decision." The UK brewing group refused to comment on industry speculation that the merger threat to jobs was the factor which helped swing the decision against Bass in the end.
